voice.text: This is AI DR, your AI news for Saturday, October tenth.
A twenty billion dollar revision rattles AI stocks, and a cap turns thoughts into prompts.

stories.headline: *OpenAI's revenue revised down*, AI stocks fall
stories.statLabel: OpenAI's September annualized revenue vs. earlier reports

voice.text: AI stocks are falling, Nvidia, Oracle and CoreWeave among them, after CNBC reported OpenAI's September annualized revenue was twenty billion dollars lower than thought.
The revision has rattled investor confidence in the AI infrastructure chain.

stories.headline: a16z leads a *big bet on AI coding*
stories.statLabel: led by a16z at a $7.5B valuation

voice.text: TypeSafe AI, maker of Jev, has raised about eight hundred seventy million dollars, led by a16z, at a seven and a half billion dollar valuation.
Sequoia joined too, a sign of investor appetite for AI coding infrastructure.
An Iranian campaign has used ChatGPT to plant fake articles in real U.S. publications.
It shows how generative AI, and AI agents, are being weaponized for influence campaigns.

stories.headline: OpenAI defends firing *three safety researchers*
stories.statLabel: safety researchers fired after an investigation

voice.text: OpenAI is defending its firing of three safety researchers, saying an investigation found they violated policies on handling sensitive information.
The firings have sparked internal concern, and criticism of the company's safety culture.

stories.headline: A cap that turns *thoughts into prompts*

voice.text: Sabi has raised fifty million dollars in seed funding for a baseball cap with a hundred thousand neuro-sensors that turn neural signals into text prompts for AI.
The goal: control AI agents through thought alone.
